speaker: Doctor
text: I'll start by asking you how long you've been experiencing these symptoms and if you have any history of recent travel or exposure to sick individuals. Additionally, have you noticed any changes in your stool or urine color?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details; the dark urine is a significant finding. Given your history of type 2 diabetes and the symptoms of fatigue, fever, and abdominal pain, have you experienced any jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes), itching, or clay-colored stools since attending the fair?

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel
REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Panel: Bilirubin_Total 3.6 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct 2.4 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase 72 U/L, AST 488 U/L, ALT 798 U/L, Hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL, Leukocyte_Count 11,600/mm3, Platelet_Count 221,000/mm3, Urea_Nitrogen 26 mg/dL, Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL, Glucose 122 mg/dL; Urinalysis: Not explicitly reported in provided data; Abdominal_Ultrasound: Not explicitly reported in provided data. General Examination confirms mild scleral icterus. Abdominal Examination confirms hepatomegaly with tenderness.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and mild fever. I also have Abdominal pain, Nausea, Dark urine. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Viral Hepatitis.

Although your previous doctor suggested appendicitis, the combination of dark urine, nausea, fatigue, and a history of potential foodborne exposure at a fair strongly points toward a liver infection. The liver function and ultrasound results we ordered will confirm whether there is inflammation of the liver and rule out other causes. Please wait for those results while we monitor your symptoms closely.
